text: The Canon EOS R50 is an entry-level APS-C mirrorless interchangeable-lens camera manufactured by Canon, announced on 27 February 2023 alongside the full-frame Canon EOS R8. It functions as an RF-mount replacement for Canon's discontinued EOS M50 Mark II and EOS 250D. Designed following the compact and lightweight principles of the EOS M50 Mark II and EOS 250D, the R50 incorporates the RF lens mount system and features from earlier EOS R series cameras, fitting the internal components of the EOS R10 into a more travel- and vlogging-friendly form factor. The camera features a 24.2-megapixel APS-C CMOS sensor, DIGIC X processor, Dual Pixel CMOS AF II focus system, and a 2.36-million-dot OLED electronic viewfinder, though physical controls have been simplified for beginner photographers. It lacks features such as a fully mechanical shutter, sensor self-cleaning, and in-body image stabilization, though in-lens stabilization is supported. The R50 includes a fully-articulating 1.62-million-dot LCD touchscreen, a built-in stereo microphone, a 3.5mm audio jack for external microphones, a UHS-I SD card slot, and built-in Wi-Fi and Bluetooth connectivity. It can shoot at 12 fps with a buffer of up to 42 JPEG images using the electronic first curtain shutter, or 15 fps with a buffer of up to 37 images using the electronic shutter, with shutter speeds ranging from 1/8000 seconds to 30 seconds. For video, it records up to 4K UHD resolution oversampled from the full sensor width at up to 29.97 fps and supports 1080p slow motion at up to 120 fps. The DIGIC X processor enables subject detection in multiple modes, up to 651 autofocus zones and 4503 autofocus points, and in-camera focus bracketing. Upon release, the EOS R50 received generally positive reviews; Engadget awarded it 87/100, calling it "a good balance between power and affordability," while Digital Photography Review gave it 84%, praising its photo and video quality and autofocus, though noting a lack of available RF-mount APS-C lenses. Some critics were more critical, with TechRadar and PCMag both giving it 3.5 stars and criticizing its ergonomics and limited physical controls, with PCMag noting the small size made it difficult to hold comfortably. On 26 March 2025, Canon introduced the EOS R50 V, a vlogging-focused variant that removes the built-in flash and electronic viewfinder but adds improved video recording capabilities, enhanced wired and wireless connectivity, and more video-oriented physical and digital controls, including the ability to shoot in Canon Log Clog3. Other Canon APS-C mirrorless cameras from the same period feature processors such as DIGIC 5/5+, DIGIC 6/6+, DIGIC 7, DIGIC 8, and DIGIC X; video capabilities including 1080p, 4K, 7K, and 8K; screen types such as flip (tilt), articulating, and touchscreen; body features like in-body image stabilization, multi-function hot shoe, and weather sealing; specialty models including astrophotography, Cinema EOS, and high-resolution cameras; and firmware add-ons like Magic Lantern Support.
